assertions.description: Removing a same-origin <iframe> from the DOM does not fire pagehide in its document (destroying a child navigable fires no pagehide). Fails while Chrome's deprecated synchronous behaviour is active.
assertions.test: (() => { const f = document.createElement('iframe'); f.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true'); f.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;left:-9999px'; document.body.append(f); let fired = false; f.contentWindow.addEventListener('pagehide', () => { fired = true; }); f.remove(); return !fired; })()

assertions.description: Removing a same-origin <iframe> does not fire unload in its document.
assertions.test: (() => { const f = document.createElement('iframe'); f.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true'); f.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;left:-9999px'; document.body.append(f); let fired = false; f.contentWindow.addEventListener('unload', () => { fired = true; }); f.remove(); return !fired; })()

assertions.description: Removing a same-origin <iframe> does not fire visibilitychange on its Document.
assertions.test: (() => { const f = document.createElement('iframe'); f.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true'); f.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;left:-9999px'; document.body.append(f); let fired = false; f.contentDocument.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { fired = true; }); f.remove(); return !fired; })()

assertions.description: Removing an ancestor element that contains a same-origin <iframe> (the framework 'clear the container' pattern) does not fire pagehide in the iframe's document.
assertions.test: (() => { const w = document.createElement('div'); w.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true'); w.style.cssText = 'position:absolute;left:-9999px'; const f = document.createElement('iframe'); w.append(f); document.body.append(w); let fired = false; f.contentWindow.addEventListener('pagehide', () => { fired = true; }); w.remove(); return !fired; })()

assertions.description: Element.prototype.moveBefore exists. It is the replacement for remove-then-reinsert re-parenting, which detaches the frame and triggers its teardown.
Navigating a subframe (not removing it) still fires pagehide and unload in the old document, in both the old and new behaviour.
assertions.test: Navigation is asynchronous and cannot be checked by a synchronous assertion. The removal-event-probe and removal-method-matrix concepts run it as their control arm (iframe.src = otherUrl) and require pagehide to arrive.

assertions.description: Chromium's flag only omits the events when the removed subframe shares an agent with the remover (it can script the ancestor DOM). An opaque sandboxed frame (sandbox=allow-scripts) keeps its teardown events.
assertions.test: This is Chromium's scoping decision (runtime_enabled_features.json5 comment and the compat study's Option 2b), not an HTML Standard requirement, and its events arrive asynchronously by postMessage. Observe it in the removal-method-matrix 'Opaque sandboxed iframe' row.
